title: Analog Scaling (Raw Counts -> Engineering Units)
concept:
An analog input arrives as RAW COUNTS, not real units. You scale it linearly to
engineering units (%, PSI, degC). For a 0-10 V channel:

    Siemens: 0 V = 0 counts,  10 V = 27648 counts
    Allen-Bradley: often 0-32767 (or module engineering-unit scaled)

Linear scale to 0-100 %:   Level := Raw * 100.0 / 27648.0;

General form:  EU := (Raw - RawMin) * (EuMax - EuMin) / (RawMax - RawMin) + EuMin.
ab_note: Studio 5000: scale with the module's engineering units, or a CPT/SCL expression on the raw tag to a REAL.
siemens_note: SCL uses NORM_X (raw -> 0.0..1.0) then SCALE_X (-> your EU range). The one-liner here does both in a single expression.

Level = Raw * 100.0 / 27648.0 (use REAL literals so it doesn't do integer math).

solution:
(* Lesson 11 -- Analog Scaling: Raw Counts -> Engineering Units *)

VAR
    Raw   : INT;    (* 0..27648 raw counts from the analog input card *)
    Level : REAL;   (* output: 0.0..100.0 engineering units (%)       *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
Level := Raw * 100.0 / 27648.0;
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
